**Wire verb `sdrf parse-age`**: Read characteristics\[age\] cells into years with an honest precision, refusing any cell that would need a guess.

# Wraps

- [`SdrfAge.TryParse`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/23c2490e/mzLib/Readers/Sdrf/SdrfAge.cs) in `mzLib/Readers/Sdrf/SdrfAge.cs` at mzLib `23c2490e`

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stdin` (wire `--stdin`) | `string[]` | required | — | `>= 1 line` | One cell per line. BLANK LINES ARE KEPT (unlike every other stdin verb) so output row i is line i; one trailing newline does not add a cell. A UTF-8 BOM is dropped. |

# Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cell_count` | `int` | cells | never | Cells read from stdin; the length of every column. |
| `parsed_count` | `int` | cells | never | Cells read as an age. |
| `columns` (wire `column_names`) | `string[]` | — | never | The table's columns. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | never | One row per input line, in order. |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | Four static caveats. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cell` | `string` | — | never | The line exactly as given (mzLib's SdrfAge.Cell is the trimmed form). |
| `years` | `float` | years | yes: the cell was refused; refusal says why | The age, a range's MIDPOINT, or a bound. |
| `min_years` | `float` | years | yes: refused | Youngest the cell allows; 0 for UpperBound. |
| `max_years` | `float` | years | yes: refused, OR precision is LowerBound: UNBOUNDED (mzLib's +infinity, which JSON cannot carry) | Oldest the cell allows. |
| `precision` | `string` | — | yes: refused | Exact (incl. degenerate 40Y-40Y since \#1333) \| Range \| LowerBound \| UpperBound. |
| `follows_specification` | `bool` | — | yes: refused | true for the spec grammar, false for unambiguous words ("3 year", "6-8 weeks", "4 hour"). |
| `refusal` | `string` | — | yes: the cell was read | empty \| reserved\_word (any case) \| no\_unit (a bare number) \| unreadable. |

# Errors

| Kind | mzLibRust returns | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | stdin empty |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | never expected: TryParse does not throw |
| `service_unavailable` | [`MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable`](crate::MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable) | never returned by this verb |

Any call can also fail on the way to mzLib or back, whatever the verb: [`MzLibError::BridgeNotFound`](crate::MzLibError::BridgeNotFound), [`MzLibError::Timeout`](crate::MzLibError::Timeout), [`MzLibError::Protocol`](crate::MzLibError::Protocol) or [`MzLibError::Io`](crate::MzLibError::Io).

# Caveats

- Units are years: month 1/12, week 7/365.25, day 1/365.25, hour 1/(365.25 x 24).
- A bare number (63, 11% of real corpus age cells) is refused, never assumed to be years.
- years for a wide Range is a poor stand-in for any one sample; filter on precision.
- Every cell costs one line, not one process: send all cells in one call.
